clue.text: Exhibit of ghoulish characters runs in gallery

parts.note: demons are ghoulish, fiendish characters

indicators.note: runs sits in the gallery, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A display of ghouls and monsters is running at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhibit' looks like a noun but is the verb. The Tate is London's best-known art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to show it openly, which is what demonstrating does; both are verbs of display.

clue.text: Does fancy ascending sequence from composer I seduced

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
a sequence taken from the words means a run of consecutive letters lifted out of them

explanation.surface: A seduced woman wonders whether she really does fancy the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sequence from' picks SERISED out of compoSER I SEDuced; 'ascending' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does fancy something wants it; the emphatic verb phrase is a synonym of the verb desires.

clue.text: Woman that's encoded as 'M'

definitions.meaning: on a cricket scorecard a ... over is recorded as M

explanation.surface: A secret code in which a woman is written down as a single letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over with no runs scored is a maiden, and bowling figures mark it with M.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old word for a girl or young unmarried woman, and M is its standard abbreviation.

clue.text: Hole where many finish short of a score

definitions.meaning: a golf course has eighteen holes; the clubhouse bar where golfers end the round is jokingly called this hole
a score is twenty, and this ordinal falls one short of twentieth

explanation.surface: A golf hole where many players finish without making a good score.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke name for the golf clubhouse bar is the 'nineteenth hole', since the course itself has only eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers finish their day in the bar, nicknamed after the hole beyond the eighteenth; and the number sits just below twenty.

clue.text: Skirt two boats unloading goods

indicators.note: unloading takes the cargo off, so the goods letters are removed from the boats
two asks for the boat word to be written twice

parts.note: a tug is a small boat that tows ships
G is a standard abbreviation for goods; both boats lose one

explanation.surface: Two boats tied up at a quay as their cargo is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles TUG to TUGTUG; 'unloading' takes out a G (goods) from each to leave TUTU.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by ballerinas, an example of a skirt.

clue.text: Computer heading getting left out repeatedly shows taste

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is dropped from the computer word

parts.note: an Apple is a make of computer

indicators.note: repeatedly means the same letter for left is dropped again, this time from the heading

parts.note: a title is a heading

explanation.surface: A computer whose heading keeps getting missed off shows poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops L from APPLE to leave APPE; 'repeatedly' drops L again, from TITLE, to leave TITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite for something is a liking or relish for it, so it is a synonym of taste in that sense.

clue.text: Top book is uplifting, it's felt

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting raises the letters so they read from the bottom up

parts.note: the top one is number one, written NO I
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A best-selling book is uplifting, and readers feel it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns NOITOME round. NO I is number one, with the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling, something that is felt rather than thought.

clue.text: Two men, one from another country

parts.note: the first of the two men, a man named Russ
the second of the two men, a man named Ian

explanation.surface: Two men meet, one of them a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two men' together supply both names, read one after the other; 'one' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian is a native of Russia, which for a British reader is a foreign land.

clue.text: Maybe square uniform sandwiches can't burst

indicators.note: the uniform word sandwiches the other letters between its parts

parts.note: regular means uniform, even

indicators.note: burst means the letters of can't break apart and come back rearranged

explanation.surface: A neat uniform, maybe square-cut, bulging because it can't burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges the letters of can't (apostrophe dropped) to CTAN, which 'sandwiches' places within the uniform word.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is one example of a rectangle, so it is rectangular; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Storm seeing fat cat caught out hanging around pub

indicators.note: the trimmed fat cat hangs around the pub, so it surrounds those letters
caught out means the letter for caught is removed

parts.note: a fat cat is a rich businessperson, a tycoon
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A wealthy businessman was seen hanging around a pub when the storm broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the C, leaving TYOON, which 'hanging around' wraps round the pub letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, a kind of violent storm.

clue.text: After tax, the woman's deposit's making flat home for a few million

definitions.text: flat home for a few million

parts.note: net income is what remains after tax
her means belonging to the woman
deposit is, read as a verb: lands, as in sets down

explanation.surface: After tax, her deposit goes toward a flat for someone worth a few million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit's' is 'deposit is' read as a verb: to land something is to deposit it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a famously low-lying, flat country with a population of some seventeen million people.

clue.text: Rogue's pocketing payment for courses

indicators.note: the rogue pockets the payment, so it holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a cur is a rogue, a contemptible man; with the s from the possessive
rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: A rogue is pocketing payment for courses he never teaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue's' keeps its S: the rogue word plus S does the pocketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Currents are flows of water or air, and a course is the path along which such a flow runs.

clue.text: Precinct detective quits firm

indicators.note: quits means the detective leaves, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a precinct is a district
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective resigns from the precinct force and quits his firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' takes DI out of DISTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being firm with someone means being strict with them, a synonym in the sense of unbending.

clue.text: Bear in the wild died or was dormant

indicators.note: in the wild, the letters run free and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A bear out in the wild either died or lay dormant through winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wild' looks like a phrase, but 'in the' is fodder and 'wild' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that hibernated spent the winter in a deep sleep, inactive and dormant.

clue.text: Too regressive, items regularly distributed in loose-leaf

indicators.note: regressive goes backwards, so the picked letters are read in reverse
regularly distributed items are every other letter of the folder word

explanation.surface: Items are being shared out evenly in a loose-leaf binder, which seems regressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items regularly distributed in' picks the even letters OSLA from lOoSeLeAf; 'regressive' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms meaning in addition, as well.

clue.text: Opposition's position is the Queen must retire first

definitions.note: Opposition's is read as Opposition is, the 's a link

indicators.note: first puts the retreating letters before the position
retiring means going back, so the two short words are read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a stance is a position

explanation.surface: The opposition's stance is that the Queen must retire first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must retire' turns ISER round to RESI; 'first' puts it before STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of opposing something, the same idea as opposition.

clue.text: Vehicles laden with Newcastle United strips seen in paper

indicators.note: laden with means loaded inside, so the vehicles carry the club letters

parts.note: cars are vehicles
the Toon is the nickname of Newcastle United football club, from the Geordie pronunciation of town

explanation.surface: Coaches packed with Newcastle United fans in their kit, as pictured in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strips' looks like football kit but means comic strips. 'laden with' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartoons are comic strips, the funny drawn panels that run in a newspaper.

clue.text: Secure stake next to electronic fence outside

indicators.note: the fence goes outside the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a guard is a protective fence or barrier

indicators.note: next to puts the electronic letter beside the stake

parts.note: an ante is a stake put in before a hand of poker
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A secure stake goes in beside the electric fence around a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the fence around the stake-plus-E. An ante is a poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Guaranteed means assured, made certain, which is what secure means as an adjective.

clue.text: Hundred broken sauce bottles — daughter held responsible

indicators.note: the sauce letters bottle up the hundred, holding it inside
broken means the letters of sauce are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred bottles of sauce are broken, and a daughter gets the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes ACUSE from SAUCE; 'bottles' puts C inside it to give ACCUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accused is charged with a wrong, held to blame for it.

clue.text: Turn over cash here?

definitions.meaning: to ... land is to turn the soil over by ploughing
the cash register in a shop

explanation.surface: A shop's turnover is kept in its cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilling a field means ploughing and turning its soil; a till is the drawer where a shop keeps money.

clue.text: Here the French will store cold frozen stuff

indicators.note: the French words will store the cold, holding it within them

parts.note: ici is French for here
les is the French plural for the
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Here, the French keep cold frozen goods in store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' covers both words: ici (here) and les (the). 'will store' puts C between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles are hanging spikes of ice, water that has frozen as it dripped.

clue.text: Dancer's equipment comes with new flat

parts.note: a barre is the handrail ballet dancers use for exercises

explanation.surface: A dancer's kit comes with a new flat to practise in.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land is flat and lifeless; flat also means dull and unproductive, like barren prose.

clue.text: See guy with energy getting pick out

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
cat is slang for a man, a guy
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Look, a guy with plenty of energy is picking things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the definition, but it is LO; the definition is 'pick out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find and identify where it is, picking it out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Country occupation the locals don't enjoy?

definitions.text: Country occupation the locals don't enjoy?

parts.words: Country occupation the locals don't enjoy?
parts.note: reads like a rural job nobody wants, but the occupation is a military one, an enemy taking over a nation

explanation.surface: A rural trade that the villagers dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country occupation' suggests a farm job; it is a whole country being occupied by an army.
explanation.definitionFit: An invasion is a hostile army entering and occupying a country, much resented by its people.

clue.text: Something fun that's unlucky, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: fate is destiny, here a doom or bad luck

explanation.surface: Something fun turns out unlucky, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: FETE is pronounced like FATE. A fete is a British outdoor fair with stalls and games, often raising money for a school or church.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a summer fair or festival, an occasion of entertainment and fun.

clue.text: Do up lounge, with shared part in shot

parts.note: to rest is to lounge about

indicators.note: the two words share their linking letter, so it is written once, dropped from the second word

parts.note: tore, as in shot or raced along

explanation.surface: Redecorating the lounge, with part of the job going into a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: REST and TORE overlap on their shared T, giving RESTORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up an old house is to renovate it, bringing it back to good condition.

clue.text: They're shelled with a twist of mussel — truthfully, that covers it

indicators.note: a twist turns the letters round so they run the other way
the two words cover the answer, holding its letters inside

explanation.surface: Shellfish with a twist of mussel; honestly, that's all there is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that covers it' finds SELTRUT inside musSEL TRUThfully; 'a twist of' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turtles are reptiles protected by a hard shell, so they are shelled creatures.

clue.text: Relative youngsters in a line

parts.note: looks like young relatives queuing, but means younger members of a family line, heirs in a lineage

explanation.surface: Young relatives standing in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a line' suggests a queue but means a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Descendants are the children, grandchildren and later offspring in a family's line of descent.
